Subjective: Ishidzu, a one and a half year old dog, presented with symptoms of head shaking and holding the head tilted to the left side for 2-3 days. The owner also reports decreased appetite during this period.
Objective: Physical examination revealed a foreign body in the left ear and yeast infection in the right ear. Ear cleaning was performed. Current medications include Easotic ear drops once daily for 5 days and Cefpodoxime syrup 3ml orally, which has been administered and advised to continue for another 5-7 days.
Assessment: The patient is diagnosed with a foreign body in the left ear and yeast infection (otomycosis) in the right ear, causing otitis externa and associated symptoms of head shaking and decreased appetite.
Plan: Continue Easotic ear drops once daily for 5 days and Cefpodoxime syrup 3ml orally for 5-7 more days. Monitor response to treatment. If symptoms persist or worsen, perform an ear swab for culture and sensitivity to guide further therapy.
Conclusion: Ishidzu is being treated for bilateral ear issues with foreign body and yeast infection. Treatment is ongoing with topical and systemic medications. Follow-up is necessary to ensure resolution.
DifferentialDiagnosis: Other causes of head shaking and ear discomfort such as bacterial otitis externa, ear mites, or neurological conditions should be considered if no improvement is seen.
KeyIssues: Foreign body in left ear, yeast infection in right ear, head shaking, decreased appetite.
AbnormalFindings: Foreign body detected in left ear, yeast growth in right ear.
